subject: maths
title: Arithmetic basics
summary: Adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing whole and negative numbers, in the right order.

subject: maths
title: Fractions and decimals
summary: A fraction is a part of a whole; decimals write the same parts in tenths.

subject: maths
title: Ratio, proportion and percentages
summary: Comparing amounts by how many times bigger; a percentage is a fraction out of 100.

subject: maths
title: Powers and roots
summary: A power is repeated multiplication; a root undoes it, like the square root of 9 is 3.

subject: maths
title: Scientific notation and significant figures
summary: Writing huge or tiny numbers as a number times a power of ten, rounded sensibly.

subject: maths
title: Algebra basics
summary: Letters stand for unknown numbers, so one rule can work for every number.

subject: maths
title: Linear equations
summary: Find the unknown by doing the same thing to both sides until it stands alone.

subject: maths
title: Rearranging formulas
summary: Move terms around a formula to make a different letter the subject.

subject: maths
title: Simultaneous equations
summary: Two equations with two unknowns: find the pair of values that makes both true.

subject: maths
title: Expanding and factorising
summary: Expanding multiplies brackets out; factorising puts the brackets back, like reverse multiplication.

subject: maths
title: Coordinates and plotting
summary: Every point on a flat grid gets an address (x, y): across, then up.

subject: maths
title: Reading graphs and slope
summary: A graph shows how one thing changes with another; slope tells how steeply it changes.

subject: maths
title: Angles and shapes
summary: Angles measure turning; a triangle's angles add to 180°, a full turn is 360°.

subject: maths
title: Pythagoras' theorem
summary: In a right triangle, the two short sides squared add up to the long side squared.

subject: maths
title: Area, circles and volume
summary: Area counts squares covering a flat shape; volume counts cubes filling a solid.

subject: maths
title: Trigonometric ratios
summary: In a right triangle, sine, cosine and tangent link an angle to side lengths.

subject: physics
title: SI units
summary: Every measurement is a number plus a unit, like 5 metres or 2 seconds.

subject: physics
title: Speed, distance and time
summary: Speed is how far you go each second: distance divided by time.

subject: physics
title: Forces and weight
summary: A force is a push or pull; weight is gravity's pull on a mass.

subject: physics
title: Energy basics
summary: Energy lets things happen; it changes form but is never made or destroyed.

subject: physics
title: Particles and states of matter
summary: Everything is made of tiny moving particles; how they pack decides solid, liquid or gas.

subject: physics
title: Density
summary: Density is how much mass is packed into each cubic metre of a material.

subject: maths
title: Sets and Venn diagrams
summary: A set is a collection of things; Venn diagrams show what sets share.

subject: maths
title: Functions, domain and range
summary: A function is a machine: each input gives exactly one output.

subject: maths
title: Composite and inverse functions
summary: Composite functions chain two machines; an inverse function runs a machine backwards.

subject: maths
title: Graph transformations
summary: Changing a function's formula slides, stretches or flips its graph.

subject: maths
title: Quadratic equations and graphs
summary: Equations with x squared; their graph is a U-shaped parabola with up to two roots.

subject: maths
title: Inequalities
summary: Inequalities say one side is bigger; their answers are ranges of numbers, not single values.

subject: maths
title: Indices and surds
summary: Rules for powers, including negative and fractional ones, and exact roots like √2.

subject: maths
title: Polynomials and the factor theorem
summary: Expressions built from powers of x; if p(a) = 0, then (x − a) is a factor.

subject: maths
title: Exponential functions
summary: Quantities that multiply by the same factor each step, like bacteria doubling every hour.

subject: maths
title: Logarithms
summary: A logarithm asks: what power gives this number? It undoes an exponential.

subject: maths
title: Radians and arc length
summary: Measuring angles by arc length divided by radius; a full turn is 2π radians.

subject: maths
title: Trig functions and the unit circle
summary: Sine and cosine as height and width on a circle, repeating every full turn.

subject: maths
title: Trigonometric identities
summary: Equations true for every angle, like sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, used to simplify.

subject: maths
title: Compound and double angles
summary: Formulas for the sine and cosine of added angles, like sin(A + B).

subject: maths
title: Solving trig equations
summary: Find every angle in a given range that makes a trig equation true.

subject: maths
title: Sine and cosine rules
summary: Rules to solve any triangle, not just right-angled ones, from known sides and angles.

subject: maths
title: Complex numbers
summary: Numbers with a real part and an imaginary part, where i squared equals −1.

subject: maths
title: Arithmetic sequences and series
summary: Lists that grow by adding the same amount each time, and their sums.

subject: maths
title: Geometric sequences and series
summary: Lists that grow by multiplying by the same amount each time, and their sums.

subject: maths
title: Permutations and combinations
summary: Counting arrangements where order matters, and selections where it doesn't.

subject: maths
title: Binomial theorem
summary: A shortcut to expand (a + b) to any whole-number power using combinations.

subject: maths
title: Straight lines
summary: Lines on a grid written as y = mx + c: slope m, crossing the y-axis at c.

subject: maths
title: Equation of a circle
summary: All points a fixed distance r from a centre (a, b): (x − a)² + (y − b)² = r².

subject: maths
title: Conic sections
summary: Parabola, ellipse and hyperbola: the curves you get by slicing a cone.

subject: maths
title: Limits
summary: The value a function gets closer and closer to as the input approaches a point.

subject: maths
title: The derivative as slope
summary: The derivative is the slope of a curve at one point: the instant rate of change.

subject: maths
title: Power rule and basic differentiation
summary: Quick slope rules: bring the power down in front, then lower the power by one.

subject: maths
title: Mean, spread and standard deviation
summary: The mean tells the centre of data; standard deviation tells how spread out it is.

subject: maths
title: Probability basics
summary: Probability says how likely something is, from 0 (never) to 1 (certain).

subject: maths
title: Vectors
summary: A vector has size and direction, drawn as an arrow; add vectors tip to tail.

subject: maths
title: Inverse trig functions
summary: Inverse sine, cosine and tangent take a ratio and give back the angle.

subject: maths
title: Matrices
summary: A matrix is a grid of numbers; matrices can be added and multiplied by set rules.

subject: maths
title: Determinants
summary: One number from a square matrix: it scales area and shows if an inverse exists.

subject: maths
title: Inverse matrices and linear systems
summary: The inverse matrix undoes a matrix, and solves several linear equations at once.

subject: maths
title: Continuity
summary: A function is continuous if you can draw its graph without lifting the pen.

subject: maths
title: Product and quotient rules
summary: Rules to differentiate two functions that are multiplied or divided together.

subject: maths
title: Chain rule
summary: Differentiate a function inside a function: outer slope times inner slope.

subject: maths
title: Derivatives of exp, log and trig
summary: The slopes of eˣ, ln x, sin x and cos x, which appear all over physics.

subject: maths
title: Implicit differentiation
summary: Differentiating equations where y is mixed in with x, like the equation of a circle.

subject: maths
title: Rates of change
summary: Using derivatives to find how fast one quantity changes when another one changes.

subject: maths
title: Maxima and minima
summary: Peaks and valleys of a smooth curve happen where its slope is zero.

subject: maths
title: Tangents and normals
summary: A tangent touches a curve at one point; a normal crosses it at right angles there.

subject: maths
title: Integration as reverse differentiation
summary: Integration undoes differentiation: find a function from its slope, plus a constant.

subject: maths
title: Definite integrals and area
summary: A definite integral adds up thin strips to find the area under a curve.

subject: maths
title: Area between curves
summary: The area between two curves is the integral of the top curve minus the bottom one.

subject: maths
title: Integration by substitution
summary: Swap a messy inner part for a new letter to make an integral simple.

subject: maths
title: Integration by parts
summary: Integrate a product of two functions by trading it for an easier integral.

subject: maths
title: Partial fractions
summary: Split one complicated fraction into simple fractions that are easy to integrate.

subject: maths
title: Differential equations
summary: Equations about rates of change; solving them gives back the function itself.

subject: maths
title: Vectors in 3D
summary: Vectors with x, y and z parts that describe position and direction in space.

subject: maths
title: Dot product
summary: Multiplying two vectors to get a number that shows how much they point the same way.

subject: maths
title: Cross product
summary: Multiplying two vectors to get a third vector at right angles to both.

subject: maths
title: Lines and planes in 3D
summary: Describing straight lines and flat planes in space with vector equations.

subject: maths
title: Complex numbers in polar form
summary: Writing a complex number as a length and an angle on the Argand diagram.

subject: maths
title: Conditional probability
summary: The probability of something when you already know something else has happened.

subject: maths
title: Discrete random variables
summary: A random variable gives a number to each outcome; its expectation is the long-run average.

subject: maths
title: Binomial distribution
summary: The chances of getting k successes in n repeated yes-or-no trials.

subject: maths
title: Normal distribution
summary: The bell-shaped curve where most values sit close to the mean.

subject: physics
title: Measurement and uncertainty
summary: Every measurement has some error; uncertainty says how far off it could be.

subject: physics
title: Dimensional analysis
summary: Checking that both sides of an equation have the same kind of units.

subject: physics
title: Scalars and vectors in physics
summary: Scalars have size only, like mass; vectors also have direction, like force.

subject: physics
title: Displacement and velocity
summary: Displacement is change in position with a direction; velocity is how fast it changes.

subject: physics
title: Acceleration
summary: Acceleration is how fast velocity changes: speeding up, slowing down or turning.

subject: physics
title: Motion graphs
summary: Slopes and areas of position-time and velocity-time graphs tell the story of a motion.

subject: physics
title: Equations of motion
summary: Four equations linking distance, velocity, acceleration and time when acceleration stays constant.

subject: physics
title: Free fall
summary: Objects falling with only gravity acting all speed up at about 9.8 m/s².

subject: physics
title: Projectile motion
summary: A thrown object moves steadily sideways while falling, tracing a curved path.

subject: physics
title: Newton's first law
summary: Things keep doing what they are doing unless an unbalanced force acts on them.

subject: physics
title: Free-body diagrams
summary: A sketch of one object with every force on it drawn as an arrow.

subject: physics
title: Newton's second law
summary: Force equals mass times acceleration; more force, more speed-up.

subject: physics
title: Newton's third law
summary: Every push on an object comes with an equal push back on the pusher.

subject: physics
title: Friction
summary: A force that resists sliding; it depends on the surfaces and how hard they press together.

subject: physics
title: Forces on a slope
summary: On a ramp, split the weight into a part along the slope and a part into it.

subject: physics
title: Momentum and impulse
summary: Momentum is mass times velocity; a force acting for a time changes it.

subject: physics
title: Conservation of momentum
summary: In collisions with no outside force, the total momentum stays the same.

subject: physics
title: Work done
summary: Work is force times the distance moved in the force's direction.

subject: physics
title: Kinetic energy
summary: Energy of movement: double the speed and the energy becomes four times bigger.

subject: physics
title: Gravitational potential energy
summary: Energy stored by height: lift something higher and it stores more energy.

subject: physics
title: Conservation of energy
summary: Energy changes form, like height into speed, but the total stays the same.

subject: physics
title: Power
summary: Power is how fast energy is transferred: joules per second, called watts.

subject: physics
title: Circular motion
summary: Moving in a circle needs a force pointing to the centre, even at steady speed.

subject: physics
title: Torque and moments
summary: Torque is the turning effect of a force: force times distance from the pivot.

subject: physics
title: Equilibrium
summary: An object is balanced when the forces cancel and the turning effects cancel too.

subject: physics
title: Rotational motion
summary: Spinning objects resist changes in spin; angular momentum stays constant without outside torque.

subject: physics
title: Newton's law of gravitation
summary: Every mass pulls every other mass; the pull weakens with distance squared.

subject: physics
title: Gravitational fields and orbits
summary: Satellites keep falling around a planet; gravity supplies the centripetal force.

subject: physics
title: Hooke's law and elasticity
summary: A spring stretches in proportion to the force, until pulled past its elastic limit.

subject: physics
title: Pressure in fluids
summary: Pressure is force per area; in a liquid it grows the deeper you go.

subject: physics
title: Buoyancy
summary: A fluid pushes up on an object with a force equal to the weight of fluid pushed aside.

subject: physics
title: Temperature and heat
summary: Temperature measures how hot something is; heat is energy flowing from hot to cold.

subject: physics
title: Specific heat capacity
summary: The energy needed to warm 1 kg of a material by 1 degree.

subject: physics
title: Latent heat
summary: Energy that changes state, like melting ice, without changing the temperature.

subject: physics
title: Conduction, convection and radiation
summary: Heat moves by particles bumping, by warm fluid moving, or by infrared radiation.

subject: physics
title: Gas laws
summary: The pressure, volume and temperature of a gas are linked: pV = nRT.

subject: physics
title: Kinetic theory of gases
summary: Gas pressure comes from particles hitting the walls; temperature tracks their average kinetic energy.

subject: physics
title: First law of thermodynamics
summary: Heat added to a gas goes into its internal energy plus the work it does.

subject: physics
title: Heat engines and the second law
summary: Heat flows from hot to cold by itself; no engine turns all its heat into work.

subject: physics
title: Simple harmonic motion
summary: Back-and-forth motion where the pull back grows with distance from the middle.

subject: physics
title: Pendulums and springs
summary: A pendulum's swing time depends on its length; a spring's on mass and stiffness.

subject: physics
title: Wave basics
summary: Waves carry energy without carrying matter; wave speed equals frequency times wavelength.

subject: physics
title: Superposition of waves
summary: When waves meet, their displacements add, so they can build up or cancel out.

subject: physics
title: Standing waves
summary: Two waves travelling opposite ways make a pattern that stays put, with nodes and antinodes.

subject: physics
title: Sound waves
summary: Sound is a wave of squashed and stretched air; its pitch is its frequency.

subject: physics
title: Doppler effect
summary: A moving source sounds higher pitched coming towards you and lower going away.

subject: physics
title: Electric charge and Coulomb's law
summary: Like charges repel and unlike charges attract; the force weakens with distance squared.

subject: physics
title: Electric field
summary: The force per coulomb a charge would feel at a point, drawn as field lines.

subject: physics
title: Electric potential and voltage
summary: Potential is energy per charge at a point; voltage is the difference between two points.

subject: physics
title: Capacitors
summary: Two plates that store charge and energy; capacitance is charge stored per volt.

subject: physics
title: Electric current
summary: Current is the flow of charge: the coulombs passing a point each second.

subject: physics
title: Resistance and Ohm's law
summary: Resistance opposes current; for many conductors, voltage equals current times resistance.

subject: physics
title: Series and parallel circuits
summary: Series parts share one path; parallel parts give the current several paths.

subject: physics
title: Kirchhoff's laws
summary: Current into a junction equals current out; voltages around any loop add to zero.

subject: physics
title: EMF and internal resistance
summary: A battery's EMF is its full push; some of it is lost inside the battery itself.

subject: physics
title: Electrical power and energy
summary: The power used by a device is voltage times current, measured in watts.

subject: physics
title: Magnetic fields
summary: Magnets and electric currents make fields that push on other magnets and currents.

subject: physics
title: Magnetic force on charges and wires
summary: Moving charges and current-carrying wires in a magnetic field feel a sideways push.

subject: physics
title: Electromagnetic induction
summary: Changing the magnetic field through a coil makes a voltage in the coil.

subject: physics
title: Lenz's law
summary: An induced current always flows so that it opposes the change that caused it.

subject: physics
title: Alternating current
summary: Current that keeps reversing direction; rms values give its effective size.

subject: physics
title: Transformers
summary: Two coils on an iron core step an alternating voltage up or down.

subject: physics
title: Electromagnetic waves
summary: Light belongs to a family of waves, from radio to gamma, all moving at light speed.

subject: physics
title: Reflection and mirrors
summary: Light bounces off a mirror at the same angle it arrives at.

subject: physics
title: Refraction
summary: Light bends when it changes speed going from one material into another.

subject: physics
title: Total internal reflection
summary: Past a critical angle, light inside glass reflects back completely instead of escaping.

subject: physics
title: Lenses
summary: Curved glass bends light to a focus, making images bigger or smaller, upright or flipped.

subject: physics
title: Interference and the double slit
summary: Light through two slits makes bright and dark stripes, showing light is a wave.

subject: physics
title: Diffraction
summary: Waves spread out when they pass through a gap or around an edge.

subject: physics
title: Polarisation
summary: Filtering a transverse wave so it vibrates in only one direction.

subject: physics
title: Photoelectric effect
summary: Light knocks electrons out of a metal only if each photon carries enough energy.

subject: physics
title: Wave-particle duality
summary: Light and electrons behave like waves in some experiments and like particles in others.

subject: physics
title: Atomic energy levels and spectra
summary: Electrons sit on energy steps; jumping between steps gives out or takes in set colours of light.

subject: physics
title: The nucleus
summary: A tiny centre of protons and neutrons that holds almost all of an atom's mass.

subject: physics
title: Radioactive decay and half-life
summary: Unstable nuclei randomly give off radiation; half-life is the time for half to decay.

subject: physics
title: Mass-energy, fission and fusion
summary: Tiny losses of mass in nuclear reactions release huge energy: E = mc².
